commits.message: fix(config): a refused file carries its payload-declaration warnings, and the comments name the merge's last word (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.5e0)

fix(config): the merge gives the payload inputs the last word, so a file's own declaration is only a warning (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.5e0)

Laying them last enforces precedence for every layer, programmatic ones
included, in the one place layers meet. The loader no longer rebuilds the
parsed file; it only names the redundant lines. A segment var under a payload
name stays refused: it stores beside the payload's input, where the merge has
no say.

fix(config): a file's own payload-input declaration is dropped with a warning, and the merge lays the payload floor beneath every base (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.5e0)

Refusing the file cost an upgrading user every other line of a config the
docs once told them to write. The floor now lives in the merge, so no base a
caller builds can lack it.

fix(config): a payload input is the daemon's, so no config can redeclare the session, file or setting the bar's own acts read (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.5e0)

The bundled default authored the payload inputs (session.id, project_dir,
config_path, every *.effective, term.cols, ...) by spreading them into its
variables, so any config file could redeclare one: `{{ .session.id }}`,
copySession and a plugin `run` then named another session.

The rows now sit beneath the parsed default instead of in it, so every
config reads them and no parsed source declares one. The loader's one
ownership check (plugin scopes) also owns the payload inputs, and refuses a
file's declaration of one, top-level or as a segment var. Synthesis no
longer supplies inputs; it only checks that its reads resolve.

Fixtures, docs and examples drop their redundant declarations; the test
floor carries the payload rows, as production does.
